### AI audit trail and zero hallucination: the evidence-or-silence rule
URL: https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/ai-audit-trail-zero-hallucination/
Published: 2026-10-14

An AI audit trail links every AI output to the specific records it retrieved, the instruction and run that produced it, and the person who reviewed it. Zero hallucination is enforced, not hoped for: under the evidence-or-silence rule, a finding that cites no record, or a number absent from its cited records, is rejected.

- Provenance means every AI output can be traced to record ids, an instruction version and a named reviewer.
- Zero hallucination is a property of the process: unsupported output is struck through, never shown as fact.
- Re-perform AI findings from the cited records; re-asking the question is not re-performance.
- Odoo 20 keeps AI conversations up to 30 days, so evidence must be moved into the record or working papers.

A finance manager asks the AI assistant how many customer invoices are more than ninety days overdue and gets a clean, confident answer. It goes into the board pack. Three weeks later the external auditor asks a plain question: which invoices? If the answer is "the AI said so", the figure is not evidence. It is an assertion with no owner.

This is the problem of provenance, and it decides whether AI output can be used in accounting and audit at all. This article sets out the rule we apply, evidence or silence, and the trail that makes it testable. It is part of our series on AI in accounting.

#### What is AI provenance in accounting and audit?

AI provenance is the recorded chain from an AI output back to the exact records it read, the instruction and run that produced it, and the person who accepted or rejected it, so that a reviewer can re-perform the work. An audit trail does the same for transactions: who created, changed, approved and posted what, and when. AI provenance extends that trail to a new kind of preparer. Without it, an AI finding cannot be traced to source, and an AI-drafted entry has a record of what was posted but not of why.

#### Why is an AI answer not audit evidence on its own?

ISA 500 requires sufficient appropriate audit evidence, and appropriateness depends on relevance and reliability. ISA 230 requires documentation that lets an experienced auditor with no prior connection to the engagement understand the work done and the evidence obtained. A fluent paragraph from a language model meets neither test unless it points to records that can be inspected. The standards are moving with the technology: in August 2026 the IAASB issued exposure drafts revising ISA 500, ISA 330 and ISA 520 to address the increased use of technology, with comments due 15 December 2026. They are not final, but the direction is clear.

Hallucination is the specific risk. A model can produce a number, a vendor name or a date that reads correctly and exists nowhere in the books. In finance this is worse than an obvious error, because it looks like the output of a calculation.

#### What does "evidence or silence" mean?

It is the operating rule of MFT Intelligence: every finding must cite the record ids the agent actually retrieved, and a finding that cites nothing, or contains a number that is not in the cited records, is rejected. Rejected findings are shown struck through, never presented as facts. The agent either shows its evidence or says nothing.

Note what the rule does not claim. It does not claim the model never errs. It moves zero hallucination from a property of the model, which nobody can guarantee, to a property of the process, which can be tested: unsupported output cannot pass as a finding.

> If the agent cannot point to the record, the finding does not exist.

##### How the check works, step by step

1. The agent retrieves records through the API, and the id of every record returned is logged.
2. The agent drafts a finding and lists the record ids it relies on.
3. A validation step checks that every cited id was actually retrieved in that run.
4. It then checks that every number, date and name in the finding appears in the cited records.
5. Any finding that fails is struck through and kept, so the reviewer sees what was rejected and why.
6. A named reviewer accepts, edits or rejects the surviving findings, and the decision is recorded.

##### A worked example

An agent reports that two bills from the same vendor carry the same reference, were posted four days apart and were both paid. It cites the two bill records and the two payment records. The validator confirms all four ids were retrieved and that the reference, dates and payment status appear in them, so the finding stands for review. In the same run the agent adds that the vendor was created by the user who approved both payments, but cites no vendor record or user log. That sentence is struck through. It may be true; it is not yet evidence, so the reviewer pulls the vendor change history before saying it.

#### What should an AI audit trail record?

| Element | Why it matters | Practical note |
| Instruction version | The same question under a different instruction gives a different answer | Odoo 20 default prompts accept context and dynamic values; version them like a policy |
| Records retrieved | The basis for re-performance | Log record ids, not only a summary of the query |
| Provider and model | Explains differences between runs | Odoo 20 selects the model automatically once you choose a provider; confirm what your database records |
| Output as delivered | Shows what the user actually saw | Keep the original, including struck-through findings |
| Reviewer and decision | Accountability sits with a person | A named, registered approver; the requester does not approve their own run |
| Resulting entry | Links the finding to the books | Draft, approval, posting; corrections by reversal, never deletion |
| Retention | Evidence must outlive the chat | Stored conversations are kept up to 30 days after the last message; copy what you need into the record or working papers |

#### Where does Odoo 20 help, and where are the gaps?

According to Odoo’s 20 release notes, several AI features point the right way. AI-powered financial insights answer questions about the company’s finances based solely on accounting data in your database, and can review suspected reconciliation errors and return findings and recommendations. Agents show live progress, can reprocess sources manually, ask before exceeding their tool call limit and request permission through buttons. Outside AI, cash journal entries are hashed on reconciliation, user group changes are logged in the user’s chatter, and bank statement attachments are available in Accounting and Documents, which keeps the source document close to the entry.

The gaps are about evidence, not capability. Conversations are kept up to 30 days, shorter than any audit cycle. Automatic model selection means a re-run may not use the same model, so re-performance should re-check the cited records rather than re-ask the question. And an answer based on accounting data is only as good as that data: if bills are miscoded, the insight repeats the error with confidence. Confirm in your own database which AI features your edition and plan include and what each run logs. More on agent behaviour in Odoo 20 AI agents under finance controls.

#### How should an auditor test an AI-generated finding?

1. Re-perform from the cited records: open each record id and confirm the facts in the finding.
2. Trace to source documents: the bill, the bank statement line and the approval, not only the ledger.
3. Test completeness: confirm the run covered the whole population for the period, not a filtered view. This is what makes full-population testing with AI defensible.
4. Review rejected findings too: a pattern of struck-through claims tells you something about the instruction or the data.
5. Document under ISA 230: what was run, on which records, who reviewed it and what was concluded.

A finding that survives these steps is a lead with evidence. It is still not a conclusion about fraud or misstatement; that judgment stays with the auditor, as we stress in AI-based fraud detection.

#### What about corrections drafted by AI?

Provenance matters most when AI moves from finding to fixing. Our rule set: agents draft correcting entries and adjustments; a named, registered person approves; above the client’s ISA 320 materiality threshold a second approver is required; corrections are made by reversal, never deletion; nothing is auto-posted. The trail then reads end to end: records retrieved, finding, draft entry, approver, posted reversal. Who may approve what is a segregation question, covered in AI and segregation of duties, and the principle is set out in agents draft, people approve.

#### Where to start on Monday

1. Pick one AI output your team already uses, such as an overdue receivables answer, and ask for the record ids behind it. If they cannot be produced, stop using it in reports.
2. Write a one-page AI evidence standard: what each run must log, who reviews it, how long evidence is kept.
3. Move any AI output used in a report or entry into the record or a working paper within the 30-day window.
4. Version the instructions of every agent that touches finance, and review changes before they go live.
5. Add a re-performance check on a few AI findings to each month-end close review.

This is the discipline behind seg-audit, MFT’s continuous audit platform. It reads the books straight from the ERP, read-only, scores every transaction by risk, and works to one rule: "No number without evidence". Findings stay on record with evidence and severity, repeats are linked to earlier findings, a finding cannot be closed without a named, registered approver, and the evidence trail is usable by external auditors. The Auditor agent applies evidence or silence today as a managed service and is being integrated into seg-audit’s report pipeline, where its output will enter a two-stage human approval chain as a draft; that integration is in final review, not yet live. For the case for continuous evidence, read what the annual audit misses in eleven months, or talk to our internal audit team.

Q: What is AI hallucination in accounting?
A: It is when an AI model produces a figure, name, date or statement that reads as correct but does not exist in the underlying records. In accounting it is dangerous because it looks like the result of a calculation. The control is to require every output to cite the records it came from and reject anything unsupported.

Q: Can AI output be used as audit evidence?
A: Only through the records it points to. ISA 500 asks for sufficient appropriate evidence, and ISA 230 asks for documentation another auditor can follow. An AI finding that cites record ids can be re-performed against those records and the source documents; an AI answer with no citations is an assertion that still needs evidence.

Q: What should an AI audit trail include?
A: At minimum: the instruction version, the ids of the records retrieved, the provider and model where available, the output as delivered including rejected findings, the named reviewer and decision, any resulting draft or posted entry, and a retention step that keeps the evidence beyond the life of the chat.

Q: How long does Odoo 20 keep AI conversations?
A: According to Odoo’s 20 release notes, stored AI conversations are kept up to 30 days after the last message. That is shorter than any audit cycle, so any AI output relied on for a report, a finding or an entry should be captured in the record or in working papers before then.

Q: Does zero hallucination mean the AI never makes mistakes?
A: No. No model can guarantee that. Zero hallucination here means a process rule: output that cites no record, or contains a number not found in its cited records, is rejected and shown struck through, so unsupported claims never reach a report as facts. A named reviewer still checks what passes.

Sources:
- Odoo, "Odoo 20 Release Notes" (24 September 2026): https://www.odoo.com/odoo-20-release-notes
- IAASB, "Project update: ISA 500, Audit Evidence" (exposure drafts, August 2026): https://www.iaasb.org/publications/project-update-isa-500-audit-evidence

### Odoo 20 AI features for accounting: a feature-by-feature map
URL: https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/odoo-20-ai-features-accounting/
Published: 2026-10-14

Odoo 20’s AI features for accounting are AI-powered financial insights, agents that create and update records inside automated and scheduled actions, a database connection through MCP, and automatic model selection, all billed per request through IAP credits. Bill line prediction and duplicate detection sit beside them. Each needs an owner, scoped access rights and a named approver.

- Every Odoo 20 AI feature consumes IAP credits billed per request; none is included in a plan.
- The financial insights assistant answers only from the accounting data already in your database.
- Agents that create or update records belong inside your approval matrix, not beside it.
- Stored AI conversations last 30 days, so file any answer that supports an entry elsewhere.

At most Odoo 20 launch demos, someone types a question about cash and gets an answer in seconds. The finance manager in the room usually asks something less exciting: which of these features read the ledger, which ones can change it, and which ones send a bill. Those three questions sort the AI items in Odoo’s 20 release notes better than any menu, and your auditor will ask them after go-live.

This article covers only the AI items and the prediction features beside them. For the full picture, read our overview of what Odoo 20 changes for finance teams and how to govern Odoo 20 AI agents in finance. Here the goal is a map you can hold against your own database.

#### What counts as an AI feature in Odoo 20 accounting?

An Odoo 20 AI feature for accounting is any function that uses an AI model to answer, draft or act on accounting data, and according to Odoo’s 20 release notes every such feature now requires credits bought through IAP (In-App Purchase), billed per request and not included in any plan. That billing rule doubles as a test: if a feature consumes credits, budget and control it as AI, whatever menu it sits in.

The AI section of the notes covers agents, agentic automation, the MCP connection and model selection; the Accounting section adds AI-powered financial insights. Bill line prediction and duplicate detection are described without being called AI. They stay on the map because they shape the same entries; whether they draw credits must be confirmed in your database.

One gap to close first: we have not verified which agent capabilities are in Enterprise and which, if any, are in Community. Confirm it for your edition and plan.

#### Which Odoo 20 AI features touch accounting, and what do they change?

"Reads" means the feature only looks at data. "Drafts" means it creates or changes records a person can still review. "Acts" means it can start work inside an automation without a person.

| Feature | What it does (per Odoo’s 20 release notes) | Credits | Effect on data | Control to put in place |
| AI-powered financial insights | Answers finance questions from accounting data in the database only; reviews suspected reconciliation errors | Yes, per request | Reads | Verify against the report before any decision or entry |
| Agentic automation | Agents run from automated and scheduled actions; chats show how errors were handled | Yes, per trigger | Acts | Owner per trigger, monthly credit review |
| Agents creating records | Create records, including from an uploaded PDF instruction file | Yes | Drafts | Draft state; approver other than the instructor |
| Agents updating records | Update records; reprocess sources | Yes | Drafts or acts, depending on rights | Minimal rights; review changes |
| Interactive responses and tool call limit | Permission requests through buttons; agent asks before exceeding its tool call limit | Yes | Gate | Decide who may grant permission |
| MCP connection | Outside tools connect to the database | Confirm | Depends on rights | Dedicated user, scoped rights, logged access |
| Automatic model selection | You choose the provider; Odoo picks the model | None stated | None directly | Record the provider; expect answers to vary |
| Stored conversations | Kept up to 30 days after the last message | Not applicable | Retention | File evidence in the approval record |
| AI file renaming (Documents) | Renames files with AI | Yes | Changes metadata | Spot-check against source |
| Bill line prediction (Accounting) | Suggests line account, tax, analytic and more from bill history | Confirm | Drafts | Review account and tax |
| Duplicate detection (Accounting) | Red for highly likely, yellow for potential duplicates | Confirm | Warns | Recorded reason for any red override |

#### What does the AI assistant actually know about your finances?

The release notes are precise on the point that matters most to accountants: the financial insights assistant answers based solely on accounting data in your database. That anchors it in your books, and it is also the limit: if bank lines are unreconciled or accruals are not yet posted, it answers from the books as they are and cannot tell you what is missing.

Before anyone quotes it in a management meeting, test it against a period you have already closed:

1. Pick a month that is closed, reconciled and reviewed, and protected by your usual lock date.
2. Write five questions whose answers you hold in signed schedules, such as receivables overdue beyond 90 days and unreconciled bank items at month end.
3. Ask each with the period and company stated, and record the answer, date and asker.
4. Compare every answer with the signed schedule and classify each difference as wording, scope (a different date, filter or entity) or substance.
5. Ask it to review suspected reconciliation errors for that month and check each finding against the Odoo 20 bank reconciliation summary report.
6. Write a one-page usage note: reliable questions, questions needing a report check, and questions not to ask.

A substance difference is not a reason to switch the feature off; it marks the boundary to write down before the first busy close.

#### How do Odoo 20 agents draft and change accounting records?

This is where AI moves from answering to doing. According to the release notes, agents can create records, including from an uploaded instruction file such as a PDF, update records, reprocess sources manually, and run inside automated and scheduled actions. An agent can be model-bound, becoming the default agent for a model, and instructions can be dictated by voice, which makes a written trail of who asked for what more important.

Confirm in your database which user and rights an agent acts under. Two Odoo 20 changes help: record rules are removed and the domain is set directly on the access right, and user group changes are logged in the user’s chatter, so widened rights leave a trail. Both belong in the review of AI agents inside segregation of duties.

Our decision rule is short. If an agent’s output can reach the general ledger, a payment or vendor master data, it stays in draft and a named person approves it. The interactive permission buttons in Odoo 20 are useful, but a click by the same person who gave the instruction is not an independent approval.

> Credits pay for the answer. They do not pay for the review, and the review is the control.

#### What do credits and conversation retention mean for finance?

Because every AI request is billed through IAP and none is included in a plan, AI cost behaves like a utility, not a licence. Budget by trigger, not by user: list each scheduled or automated action that calls an agent with its frequency, and compare consumption with that list monthly. Consumption you cannot map points to a trigger nobody owns.

Automatic model selection means the model behind an answer can change without any configuration change on your side, so record the provider in your AI policy and do not expect identical answers on different dates. Stored conversations are kept up to 30 days after the last message. If a conversation supports an entry or a decision, copy the answer into the approval record on the entry, and see our note on the audit trail for AI output.

#### Which features predict rather than reason, and why does it matter?

These Accounting features shape entries as much as any agent, so they belong in the same review.

##### Bill line prediction

When a bill is encoded manually or by import, Odoo suggests the product, account, tax, analytic distribution and vehicle from bill history and the label. Prediction from history repeats history, mistakes included: a vendor miscoded for a year will be miscoded again with confidence. Test it on vendors whose coding you recently corrected. For the wider entry workflow, see automating journal entries and bank reconciliation with AI.

##### Duplicate detection and pending payments

The payment wizard also detects pending payments to prevent double payment. A warning becomes a control only when overrides are recorded with a reason, by someone authorised to override.

#### What should a finance team do on Monday?

1. List every AI feature enabled in your database, using the table above as the checklist, and confirm which are available in your edition and plan.
2. Name one owner for the IAP credit balance and one approver for each agent that can create or update accounting records.
3. Run the closed-month test of the financial insights assistant and write the usage note.
4. Review access rights for every user or connection used by agents or MCP, and read the chatter for recent group changes.
5. Sample 20 predicted bill lines and every red duplicate warning overridden in the last month.
6. Decide where AI answers that support entries are filed, so the evidence outlives the 30-day conversation window.

If you are still planning the move, fold these checks into your Odoo 20 upgrade plan, and follow the step-by-step guide to applying AI accounting on Odoo 20 for the rollout sequence. The series hub covers what AI in accounting means in practice, and a companion piece covers connecting AI to Odoo for continuous auditing.

It is the same rule our own MFT Intelligence agents follow: agents draft, a named person approves, and nothing is posted automatically.

Q: Do Odoo 20 AI features cost extra?
A: Yes. According to Odoo’s 20 release notes, all AI features require credits purchased through IAP (In-App Purchase). Credits are billed per request and are not included in any plan, so scheduled agents consume credits each time they run, whether or not they find anything useful.

Q: Can the Odoo 20 AI assistant answer questions about my company’s finances?
A: Yes. AI-powered financial insights answers questions about topics such as receivables, cash flow and reconciliation issues, based solely on the accounting data in your database. It can also review suspected reconciliation errors and return findings. Its answers are only as complete as your books, so verify them against reports.

Q: Is bill line prediction in Odoo 20 an AI feature?
A: The release notes list bill line prediction in the Accounting section. It suggests product, account, tax, analytic and vehicle from bill history and the bill label. Whether it consumes IAP credits should be confirmed in your own database. Either way, it repeats past coding, so predicted lines need review.

Q: Are Odoo 20 AI agents available in Community edition?
A: We could not verify the edition split for AI agents from the Odoo 20 release notes. Confirm with Odoo or your implementation partner which agent capabilities your edition and plan include before you design any accounting process around them, and budget for IAP credits in either case.

Q: How long does Odoo 20 keep AI conversations?
A: According to the Odoo 20 release notes, stored conversations are kept up to 30 days after the last message. If an AI answer supports a journal entry, an adjustment or a decision, copy it into the record where the approval sits, so the evidence survives after the conversation is gone.

Sources:
- Odoo, "Odoo 20 Release Notes" (official release notes, September 2026): https://www.odoo.com/odoo-20-release-notes

### Connecting AI to Odoo for continuous auditing: access, evidence and approvals
URL: https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/connect-ai-to-odoo-continuous-audit/
Published: 2026-10-14

To connect AI to Odoo for continuous auditing, give the analysis layer its own dedicated user with read access only, through the external API or the MCP connection listed in Odoo’s 20 release notes. Keep client data on the client’s system, make every finding cite the record ids it read, and route any proposed correction to a named approver.

- The audit connection gets its own user, its own key and read access only.
- Ask where data is processed and stored before asking what the model can do.
- A finding without the record ids behind it is an opinion, not evidence.
- Corrections are drafted by the system and approved by a named person, never posted by the connection.

Picture a familiar year-end conversation: the auditor finds a vendor paid twice in the second quarter, the board asks why nobody noticed, and the honest answer is that the payment sat in Odoo for nine months while everyone waited for the annual audit. We wrote about that gap in why an annual audit misses eleven months. The fix is not more auditors. It is a connection that reads the books every day and raises the question while the money can still be recovered.

Connecting AI to an ERP is easy to demonstrate and easy to get wrong: the connection is a new user that sees everything the auditor sees, often run by a third party, often processing data outside the company. This article sets out the design decisions in the order an auditor would check them.

#### What does connecting AI to Odoo for continuous auditing mean?

Connecting AI to Odoo for continuous auditing means giving an analysis layer governed, logged and read-only access to the ledger, so that tests run on the full population on a schedule and every result points back to the records it came from. Two words in that definition carry the weight. Governed means someone owns the connection, its rights and its output. Points back means a finding can be reopened in Odoo by anyone who doubts it.

It fits the monitoring component of COSO’s Internal Control, Integrated Framework (2013): Principle 16 calls for ongoing and separate evaluations, and a daily test run is an ongoing evaluation. For how this differs from the annual cycle, see continuous auditing with AI vs traditional auditing.

#### Which connection route should you use: API, MCP or in-database agents?

Three routes lead into the data and one goes around it, each with its own control profile.

| Route | How it reaches the data | Best suited to | Main control |
| External API (XML-RPC / JSON-RPC) | A dedicated API user and key query the database; long available in recent Odoo versions, confirm in your 20 database | Scheduled full-population tests run by an outside platform | Dedicated user, read-only rights, key rotation, access log review |
| MCP connection | Odoo’s 20 release notes list connecting to the database via Model Context Protocol, so AI tools can query it | Interactive questions from an AI assistant during an engagement | Confirm in your database which user and rights it runs under before enabling |
| Odoo’s own AI agents | Agents run inside the database, triggered by automated or scheduled actions | Operational checks owned by the finance team | Agent owner, draft state for output, IAP credit budget |
| Exports and spreadsheets | Someone extracts data and sends a file | One-off analysis | Completeness check against the trial balance; no ongoing coverage |

For continuous auditing the external API is usually the backbone, because it is independent of the people being audited and can run on a fixed schedule. MCP is useful for an auditor asking follow-up questions, but treat it as a new access path with its own approval, not as a feature to switch on. The finance-side view of these features is in our feature map of Odoo 20 AI for accounting.

#### Why should the audit connection read only?

Because the auditor must not be able to change what the auditor tests. If the connection can write, a finding and its fix can come from the same identity, which breaks the segregation of duties the audit is meant to test. ISA 315 (Revised 2019) asks auditors to understand the IT environment and general IT controls; an audit connection with write rights is exactly the kind of access that understanding should flag.

1. Create a dedicated user for the connection. Never reuse a person’s login or an administrator account.
2. Grant read access only to the models the tests need: journal entries, invoices and bills, payments, partners, products and stock valuation.
3. In Odoo 20, record rules are removed and the domain is set directly on the access right, so review that domain as part of the setup.
4. Issue an API key for that user alone and record who holds it and when it will be rotated.
5. Review the user’s chatter monthly: Odoo 20 logs user group changes there, so any widening of rights leaves a trail.
6. Test the restriction: attempt a write with the key and file the refusal as evidence that read-only holds.

Read-only applies to the connection, not to everything AI does. MFT’s seg-audit platform reads the books straight from the ERP, read-only. Our Auditor agent does more: it drafts correcting entries and adjustments, but drafting is not posting, and nothing reaches the ledger without approval. For segregation of duties when an agent is in the chain, see AI, segregation of duties and internal controls.

#### Where does the data go, and who keeps it?

Data residency is the question owners ask last and should ask first. A connection that copies the whole ledger to an outside store creates a second set of books, outside your controls and possibly outside your country. Ask every provider, including us, the same questions:

- Is client data stored by the provider, or read at query time and discarded?
- In which country is it processed, and by which AI model provider?
- How long are prompts, answers and logs kept, and can they be deleted on request?
- Who at the provider can see the data, and is that access logged?
- Does the provider’s contract match your data-protection obligations, as confirmed by your legal adviser?

Our own answer is that client data stays on the client’s system and our agents read through the API at query time. Odoo’s native AI has its own retention rule: according to the release notes, stored conversations are kept up to 30 days after the last message. Know both rules before anything goes live.

#### Which tests should run continuously?

Start with tests whose exceptions are cheap to verify and expensive to miss. These are the patterns that recur in our continuous-audit work:

- Duplicate and near-duplicate payments: same vendor, similar amount and reference, close dates.
- Near-duplicate vendors: similar names, shared bank accounts or tax numbers.
- Approvals outside the approval matrix: bills or orders approved above the approver’s limit.
- Cut-off errors: receipts and bills recorded in different periods around month end.
- Inventory valuation drift between the stock valuation and the general ledger.
- Manual journal entries posted late at month end in round amounts, which ISA 240 already requires auditors to test.

Each test reads the whole population, not a sample, which is the subject of moving from sampling to full-population testing. The ACFE’s 2024 Report to the Nations found the median fraud lasted 12 months before detection, and that proactive data monitoring and analysis was among the controls associated with roughly half the losses and duration. A daily test proves nothing alone; it shortens how long a problem stays hidden.

#### How does an AI finding become audit evidence?

Only by pointing at the records. ISA 500 asks whether evidence is sufficient and appropriate, and ISA 230 asks that documentation let an experienced auditor understand what was done. An AI sentence meets neither. A finding that lists the record ids it retrieved, the rule that flagged them and the time of the query meets both, because anyone can reopen those records in Odoo.

> If a finding cannot name the records it read, it is not a finding. It is a rumour with a confidence score.

That is the rule MFT Intelligence runs on, which we call "evidence or silence": every finding must cite the record ids the agent actually retrieved, and a finding that cites nothing, or quotes a number not in the cited records, is rejected and shown struck through, never as fact. The details are in our article on AI provenance and the zero-hallucination principle. The standards are moving too: in August 2026 the IAASB issued exposure drafts revising ISA 500, ISA 330 and ISA 520 to address greater use of technology, with comments due 15 December 2026. They are not final, so build on the current standards.

#### Who approves what the AI proposes?

A named, registered person, never the connection and never the person who asked for the run. Our rule set, described in agents draft, people approve, is:

- The agent drafts the correcting entry or adjustment; nothing is posted automatically.
- Approval is tiered by the client’s ISA 320 materiality threshold: above it, a second approver signs.
- Corrections are made by reversal, never by deletion, so the original stays visible.
- In seg-audit, a finding cannot be closed without a named, registered approver, and repeats are linked to earlier findings.

Live Odoo write-back of approved corrections is delivered per client, only after that client’s connector is configured. Until then, approved corrections are entered by the client’s own team, which keeps the posting under their controls.

#### Where should you start?

1. Write down the purpose of the connection, its owner and the tests it will run.
2. Create the dedicated read-only user and key, and test that a write is refused.
3. Get written answers to the five residency questions above.
4. Run three tests on a closed quarter first, such as duplicate payments, near-duplicate vendors and late round-amount journal entries, and calibrate false positives.
5. Agree who reviews exceptions, in what time frame, and who approves corrections.
6. Review the connection’s log, rights and findings monthly, as you would any privileged user.

This is the work behind our internal audit service: seg-audit reads the books read-only, scores every transaction by risk instead of sampling a few percent, and keeps each finding on record with evidence and severity. If your Odoo 20 rollout is still ahead, combine this with the step-by-step guide to AI accounting on Odoo 20.

Q: Can AI connect directly to Odoo?
A: Yes. Recent Odoo versions offer an external API (XML-RPC and JSON-RPC) used with a dedicated API user and key, and Odoo’s 20 release notes add connecting to the database via MCP (Model Context Protocol). Confirm in your own database which user and rights each connection runs under before enabling it.

Q: Should an audit AI have write access to Odoo?
A: No. The connection used for continuous auditing should read only, so the tool that tests the books cannot change them. If an AI system proposes corrections, they should arrive as drafts approved by a named person, with corrections made by reversal rather than deletion.

Q: Does connecting AI to Odoo move my data outside the company?
A: It depends on the provider. Some copy the ledger to their own storage; others read through the API at query time. Ask where data is processed, by which model provider, how long prompts and logs are kept, and who can see them, and have your legal adviser check the contract.

Q: Can AI findings be used as audit evidence?
A: Only when they trace to records. A finding that lists the record ids retrieved, the rule applied and the time of the query can be reopened and verified, which is what ISA 500 and ISA 230 expect. An unsupported AI statement is not evidence, however confident it sounds.

Q: What should continuous auditing test first in Odoo?
A: Start with tests that are cheap to verify and costly to miss: duplicate and near-duplicate payments, near-duplicate vendors, approvals outside the approval matrix, cut-off errors, inventory valuation drift, and manual journal entries posted late at month end in round amounts. Run them on a closed period first to calibrate.

Sources:
- Odoo, "Odoo 20 Release Notes" (official release notes, September 2026): https://www.odoo.com/odoo-20-release-notes
- ACFE, "Occupational Fraud 2024: A Report to the Nations" (report, 2024): https://www.acfe.com/en-us/-/media/files/acfe/pdfs/rttn/2024/2024-report-to-the-nations.pdf
- IAASB, "Project update: ISA 500 Audit Evidence" (exposure drafts on ISA 500, ISA 330 and ISA 520, August 2026): https://www.iaasb.org/publications/project-update-isa-500-audit-evidence

### Odoo 20 purchase approvals: automate the matrix, keep the control
URL: https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/odoo-20-purchase-approvals-automation/
Published: 2026-10-14

To automate purchase approvals in Odoo 20, write the approval matrix first, then map each row to a mechanism: the Purchase Order Approval setting for order thresholds, the Approvals app for categories and several approvers, and automation rules with activity plans for vendor changes. Let AI agents draft records only, and test every month for split orders and bypasses.

- Design the approval matrix on paper, with tiers taken from materiality, before changing any setting.
- Use blocking mechanisms where cash is at stake and activities where data is at stake.
- Odoo 20 changes purchasing comparisons, dates and bill matching, not the approval settings.
- An AI agent drafts purchasing records; its user never sits in an approver group.

The purchase approval that fails most often is the one configured on the wrong document. A manager’s validation is set on orders above a threshold, and the threshold quietly becomes a target: two orders just below it instead of one above it, a bill entered with no order at all, a vendor’s bank account changed by the same person who releases payments. Approvals outside the approval matrix are a recurring finding in our continuous-audit work, and few involve a broken setting.

Odoo 20 adds AI agents that run from automated actions, and several purchasing and payables improvements. Neither replaces the approval matrix. Here is how to build that matrix into Odoo 20 so that automation routes, AI drafts, and the evidence of who approved what survives an audit.

#### What is purchase approval automation in Odoo 20?

Purchase approval automation is the set of ERP rules that routes each purchase request, order, bill and vendor change to an authorised approver by amount, category and risk, holds the next step until approval is recorded, and keeps that record as evidence. Automation routes and blocks; a person decides. There are three layers:

- The rule: who may approve what, up to which tier, independent of whom. Finance owns it.
- The mechanism: the Odoo setting, app or automation that applies the rule to a document.
- The evidence: the chatter entry, approval record, activity or signature showing a named person applied the rule on a date.

#### How do you build the approval matrix before configuring anything?

Start from events, not screens. A purchase cycle has six events that can need approval: the need, the commitment, the receipt, the bill, a vendor master change, and the payment. For each, decide the trigger, the approver, and whose work that approver must be independent of. Set the amount tiers from your planning materiality, as discussed in setting a materiality threshold under ISA 320, rather than from round numbers chosen at go-live.

| Event | Approval trigger | Approver (independent of) | Odoo mechanism to confirm in your 20 database | Evidence kept |
| Non-routine request | Spend outside replenishment rules | Budget owner (not the requester) | Approvals app category (Enterprise) | Approval record |
| Purchase order, tier 1 | Order total above the first tier | Purchasing manager (not the buyer) | Purchase Order Approval setting | Validation in the order chatter |
| Purchase order, tier 2 | Above the second tier, capital spend, or new vendor | Finance manager (second approver) | Approvals app, or automation rule triggering an activity plan | Approval record or completed activity |
| Vendor creation or bank change | Every change | Finance reviewer (not purchasing, not payments) | Automation rule triggering a review activity plan | Completed activity, vendor chatter |
| Vendor bill | No order, or outside tolerance | Payables lead (not the buyer) | Bill control on received quantities, order matching, duplicate warnings | Match summary, resolved warning |
| Payment | Every batch | Treasury approver (not the payables clerk) | Payment rights limited to a named group | Payment record and bank confirmation |

Two rules make the matrix hold. The approver is independent of the work approved, as covered in segregation of duties in Odoo and, once agents act in the system, of AI agents inside segregation of duties. And every row names its evidence: an approval nobody can show did not happen.

#### Which Odoo mechanism should carry which approval?

These are long-standing features; confirm each one’s behaviour in your own Odoo 20 database and edition.

##### The Purchase Order Approval setting

In recent Odoo versions, the Purchase settings include an order approval option: orders above an amount you set need a manager’s validation before confirmation. It sits on the document, which makes it good evidence. Its limits are clear: one amount for all categories, one level, and nothing that stops a split order or a bill without an order.

##### The Approvals app

In recent Odoo versions, the Approvals app (Enterprise) lets you define approval categories with their approvers, for example capital purchases or a first order with a new vendor. It suits requests before an order and cases needing several approvers. Odoo’s 20 release notes contain no Approvals app section, so expect it to behave as before, and test it anyway.

##### Automation rules, activity plans and Sign

According to Odoo’s 20 release notes, automation rules can now trigger activity plans, and Sign supports automated signature requests with fixed and role-based signers, sent from activities or activity plans, with Arabic script supported. A practical use: a vendor bank account change triggers a plan with a finance review, a call-back on a known number, and a signed confirmation. An activity does not by itself block the next step; where a step must be blocked, use a mechanism that blocks, or a small documented customisation.

The decision rule we apply: use a blocking mechanism where cash is at stake, an activity where data is at stake, and a signature where an external or legal acknowledgement is needed.

#### What does Odoo 20 change in purchasing and payables?

Odoo’s 20 release notes list no change to purchase approval settings. The Purchase changes concern comparison, dates and cost, and several improve what an approver sees:

- An alternatives comparison screen: evidence that alternatives were considered above your upper tier.
- An editable expected arrival date that keeps the vendor’s original date for on-time rates, and recomputed arrival when the deadline has passed.
- A vendor quality rate based on quality checks.
- Sections and notes in purchase agreements and blanket orders, totals on order sections, and a default Incoterm per vendor.

In payables, the release notes add purchase order matching improvements (auto-complete, a match summary and unmatch), matching rules with payment tolerance, red and yellow duplicate warnings, and a payment wizard that detects pending payments. Treat unmatch as a control point: restrict it and review its use monthly. Two access changes also matter: record rules are removed and the domain is set on the access right itself, and user group changes are logged in the user’s chatter, so re-check every approver group after the upgrade. The wider picture is in Odoo 20 for finance teams, and the matching logic in the three-way match.

#### Where does AI fit in purchasing approvals?

AI drafts; approval stays human. According to Odoo’s 20 release notes, agents can be triggered by automated and scheduled actions, create records (including from an uploaded instruction file such as a PDF), update records, ask permission through buttons, and ask before exceeding their tool call limit. Bill line prediction suggests product, account, tax and analytic from bill history and the label. All AI features need IAP credits billed per request; confirm which agent features your edition and plan include. The release notes describe no purchasing-specific agent.

- Drafting a request for quotation from a vendor’s quotation file: it stays in draft, the buyer reviews it, and the matrix applies as for any order.
- A scheduled agent drafting a weekly list of orders close to a tier, by vendor: useful only if each line cites the orders it read.
- Bill line prediction: track how often reviewers change suggested accounts, and keep review mandatory until that rate is stable and low.

The agent’s user must never sit in an approver group, the principle behind agents draft, people approve. For every AI item and its credit model, see the Odoo 20 AI feature map for accounting.

#### How do you test that approvals are not being bypassed?

ACFE’s 2026 Report to the Nations found that more than half of fraud cases involved a lack of internal controls or an override of existing ones. A purchase matrix is overridden in predictable ways, each leaving a trace in the ledger. Run these tests on the full population, not a sample, as explained in moving from sampling to full-population testing:

1. Split orders: group confirmed orders by vendor within a short window, such as seven days, and flag groups whose combined total crosses a tier while each order stays below it.
2. Bills without orders for vendors or products that normally go through purchasing.
3. Orders created or confirmed after the date of the bill they support.
4. Approver equals requester or buyer on the same order.
5. A vendor bank change followed by a payment before the review activity was completed.
6. Bills unmatched and rematched, and red duplicate warnings overridden without a recorded reason.

A worked example of the first test: if the first tier is T, three orders to one vendor within five days, each at 90% of T, will pass the setting individually and represent 270% of T together. The setting worked; the matrix did not.

> An approval limit that is never tested for splitting becomes a price list for avoiding approval.

#### Where should you start on Monday?

1. Export users and groups, and list who can confirm orders, validate bills, change vendors and release payments.
2. Write the matrix on one page, with tiers derived from materiality, and have finance sign it.
3. Map each row to a mechanism and mark it as blocking or reminder.
4. Configure it in a test database and run the bypass tests on last quarter’s data.
5. Only then add AI drafting, with a named owner for IAP credits and approvers outside the agent’s group.

This sequence fits the wider rollout in applying AI accounting on Odoo 20 step by step, and the tests can run continuously once you connect AI to Odoo for continuous auditing. In our Odoo ERP implementations, the matrix is signed before users are created. seg-audit, our continuous audit platform, reads the books read-only and scores every transaction by risk; approvals outside the matrix are among the patterns it surfaces. A Procurement agent is in internal validation within MFT Intelligence; like all our agents, it drafts and a named person approves.

Q: Does Odoo 20 have purchase order approval?
A: In recent Odoo versions, the Purchase settings include an order approval option where orders above a set amount need a manager’s validation before confirmation. Odoo’s 20 release notes list no change to it, so it should behave as before, but confirm the setting and its effect in your own Odoo 20 database before go-live.

Q: Can Odoo handle multi-level purchase approvals?
A: The built-in order approval setting has one amount and one level. For several tiers or approvers, recent Odoo versions offer the Approvals app in Enterprise with approval categories, and automation rules that can trigger activity plans. Where a step must be blocked rather than reminded, test the behaviour or use a small documented customisation.

Q: Is there an AI agent for purchasing in Odoo 20?
A: Odoo’s 20 release notes describe general AI agents that can create and update records and run from automated or scheduled actions, but no agent specific to purchasing. You can configure an agent to draft purchasing records, provided the output stays in draft and a person outside the agent’s group approves it.

Q: How do you stop purchase order splitting in Odoo?
A: A threshold alone cannot stop it, because each split order is below the limit. Group confirmed orders by vendor within a short window and flag groups whose combined total crosses a tier. Run the test monthly on the full population, and review flagged groups with the approver who should have seen them.

Q: Do AI features in Odoo 20 cost extra?
A: Yes. According to Odoo’s 20 release notes, all AI features require credits bought through In-App Purchase, billed per request and not included in any plan. Agents triggered on a schedule consume credits each time they run, so name an owner for the credit balance and review consumption by agent every month.

Sources:
- Odoo, "Odoo 20 Release Notes" (September 2026): https://www.odoo.com/odoo-20-release-notes
- ACFE, "Occupational Fraud 2026: A Report to the Nations" (press release, 19 May 2026): https://www.acfe.com/about-the-acfe/newsroom-for-media/press-releases/press-release-detail?s=report-to-the-

### AI accounting on Odoo 20, step by step: a 90-day rollout with gates
URL: https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/odoo-20-ai-accounting-step-by-step/
Published: 2026-10-14

To apply AI accounting on Odoo 20, roll it out in three 30-day phases with a gate between each: first assistive features such as bill line prediction and financial insights, then AI in bank reconciliation, then agents that draft entries for approval. Each gate requires measured error rates, named approvers and retained evidence before the next phase starts.

- Measure today’s error and backlog figures before enabling anything, or no gate can be passed honestly.
- Start with features that suggest, move to features that match, and finish with agents that draft.
- Every gate has a stop rule written in advance, not decided after the results arrive.
- Agent conversations are kept up to 30 days, so export what your audit file needs.

Gartner’s 2025 survey of finance leaders found that 59% use AI in their finance function, almost unchanged from 58% a year earlier, after a sharp rise from 37% in 2023. The barriers cited were complexity, data and talent. In our experience the stall rarely comes from the model. It comes from the order of work: a team switches on several AI features at once, cannot tell which one produced which error, and quietly returns to doing things by hand.

Odoo 20 puts a broad set of AI features inside the accounting application. This guide is the procedure we use to bring them in one layer at a time, over roughly 90 days, with a gate between phases that must be passed on evidence.

#### What does applying AI accounting on Odoo 20 mean?

AI accounting on Odoo 20 is the controlled use of Odoo’s AI features, and of external AI agents connected to the database, to suggest, match, explain and draft accounting records, with every output reviewed by a named person before it affects the ledger. According to Odoo’s 20 release notes, the relevant features include:

- Bill line prediction: product, account, tax and analytic suggested from bill history and the label.
- AI-powered financial insights: questions about receivables, cash flow or reconciliation issues, answered solely from the accounting data in your database, including a review of suspected reconciliation errors.
- Agentic automation: agents triggered by automated and scheduled actions that create and update records.
- A connection to the database through MCP (Model Context Protocol) for outside AI tools.

All AI features require IAP credits, billed per request and not included in any plan. Confirm which agent features your edition and plan include before you design around them. The full inventory is in the Odoo 20 AI feature map for accounting.

#### What must be true before day 1?

Day 0 is the step most teams skip, and it decides whether the gates mean anything.

- Version and support: Odoo 17.0 standard support was planned to end in September 2026. If you are still on it, finish the upgrade plan before adding AI.
- Chart of accounts: in Odoo 20 parent accounts replace account groups and account codes become optional. Settle your coding policy first, because bill line prediction learns from history, including history you would rather it forgot.
- Access rights: record rules are removed and the domain sits on the access right, and group changes are logged in the user’s chatter. Redesign roles, then create a separate user for each agent.
- Status names: payment statuses are renamed (In Process becomes Paid, Paid becomes Reconciled). Update reports, filters and any prompt that refers to them.
- Lock dates: in recent Odoo versions lock dates protect closed periods; set them and restrict who can change them.
- Credits: name an owner for the IAP balance and set a monthly ceiling in requests.
- Baseline: record today’s days to close, unreconciled bank items by age, and the share of bills corrected after entry.

#### Days 1 to 30: which AI features should you switch on first?

Start with features that suggest and leave the person in control of every posting. Bill line prediction and financial insights fit this description; so does bill digitization, which in recent Odoo versions reads bills by OCR using IAP credits. The work in this phase is measurement:

1. Enable bill line prediction for one journal or one group of vendors, not all at once.
2. For every bill in the pilot, the reviewer records whether each suggested account, tax and analytic was accepted, changed or removed.
3. Ask the financial insights assistant the same five questions each week, and tie every answer back to the standard report it should agree with.
4. Log every disagreement with its cause: stale history, a miscoded vendor, or a wrong answer.

A worked example of the rule we apply: a changed analytic is an inconvenience, a changed account is a classification error, and a changed tax is a compliance error. Score them separately. A pilot can pass with frequent analytic corrections and fail on a handful of tax corrections.

#### Days 31 to 60: how do you bring AI into bank reconciliation?

Reconciliation is where Odoo 20 changes the most. According to Odoo’s 20 release notes, entries affecting bank accounts must now originate from bank transactions, matching rules support a payment tolerance and a matching order, Auto Reconciliation can be run manually, and a summary report shows reconciled and unreconciled items at period end. The AI assistant can review suspected reconciliation errors and return findings and recommendations.

1. Write the matching rules on paper first: which fields, what tolerance, in what order. Approve them as you would a policy.
2. Run Auto Reconciliation manually on a closed month and compare the result with the reconciliation you signed at the time.
3. Ask the assistant to review the remaining unreconciled items, and have a person resolve each recommendation with a recorded reason.
4. File the summary report in the close pack, signed by preparer and reviewer, as set out in the month-end close checklist.

The control detail sits in Odoo 20 bank reconciliation and bill payments, and the AI angle in automating journal entries and bank reconciliation with AI.

#### Days 61 to 90: when may agents start drafting?

Only now, and only in draft. According to Odoo’s 20 release notes, agents can be triggered by automated and scheduled actions, an agent can become the default agent for a model, agent questions and permission requests are answered through buttons, and the agent asks before exceeding its tool call limit. Stored conversations are kept up to 30 days after the last message.

- Choose one narrow use, such as drafting accrual reversals or recurring entries, and give the agent its own user with the minimum rights.
- Keep every output in draft; approval is tiered by materiality, with a second approver above your threshold.
- Export the conversation and the records it cited into the close file before the retention period ends, because ISA 230 expects documentation an experienced auditor can follow.
- Correct by reversal, never by deletion, so the audit trail shows both the draft and the fix.

If an external reviewer will read the books continuously, plan that link with connecting AI to Odoo for continuous auditing. The evidence principle behind all of it is in evidence or silence.

> Switch on one AI feature at a time, and only after you can measure what it got wrong.

#### What does each gate have to prove?

COSO’s Principle 16 calls for ongoing and separate evaluations of whether controls are working. The gates are those evaluations, made explicit. Each one has a stop rule agreed before the phase starts.

| Phase | Scope | Owner | Evidence to pass the gate | Stop rule |
| Day 0 | Version, chart of accounts, roles, lock dates, credits, baseline | Finance manager | Signed role matrix, recorded baseline | No baseline, no start |
| Days 1 to 30 | Bill line prediction, financial insights, bill digitization | Payables lead | Correction rates by account, tax and analytic; insight answers tied to reports | Any unexplained tax correction pattern |
| Days 31 to 60 | Matching rules, Auto Reconciliation, AI review of reconciliation errors | Treasury or GL accountant | Signed summary report; closed-month rerun agrees with the signed reconciliation | An automatic match reversed on review without explanation |
| Days 61 to 90 | One agent drafting one entry type | Controller | Every draft approved or rejected by a named person; conversations exported | Any agent output posted without approval |
| After 90 | Second agent or wider scope | Finance manager with internal audit | Quarterly review of rights, credits and rejected drafts | Credit use without an owning agent |

A stop rule pauses the phase, not the project. Fix the cause, rerun the measurement, and reopen the gate.

#### Where should you start on Monday?

1. Confirm your Odoo version, edition and plan, and what each includes for AI.
2. Record the baseline figures before anyone changes a setting.
3. Pick one journal for the bill line prediction pilot and one reviewer to score it.
4. Write the three stop rules and have the finance manager sign them.
5. Book the day-30 gate review now, with someone from outside the pilot in the room.

The same gated approach applies to purchasing, covered in automating purchase approvals in Odoo 20, and the broader context is in our guide to AI in accounting and AI in the monthly close. MFT runs this rollout as part of our Odoo ERP work. Our Auditor agent and Virtual CFO agent are available as a managed service: they draft, a named and registered person approves, and nothing is auto-posted.

Q: How long does it take to implement AI accounting in Odoo 20?
A: A controlled rollout takes about 90 days for a typical finance team: 30 days for assistive features such as bill line prediction, 30 for AI in bank reconciliation, and 30 for a first agent that drafts entries. The time goes into measuring errors and passing gates, not into switching features on.

Q: Which Odoo 20 AI feature should accounting enable first?
A: Start with features that suggest and leave a person in control of posting, such as bill line prediction and the AI-powered financial insights assistant. Pilot them on one journal, record every correction by type, and check each assistant answer against the standard report it should agree with.

Q: Can Odoo 20 AI agents post journal entries automatically?
A: According to Odoo’s 20 release notes, agents can create and update records and run from automated or scheduled actions. Whether their output reaches the ledger without review is a control you design. We keep agent output in draft, require a named approver tiered by materiality, and correct errors by reversal.

Q: How long does Odoo 20 keep AI agent conversations?
A: Odoo’s 20 release notes state that stored conversations are kept up to 30 days after the last message. If a conversation supports an accounting entry or a close decision, export it with the records it cited into your close file before that period ends, so the evidence survives for the auditor.

Q: What should we measure before starting AI in accounting?
A: Record a baseline before changing any setting: days to close, unreconciled bank items by age, and the share of bills corrected after entry. Without a baseline you cannot show that a phase improved anything, and no gate in the rollout can be passed on evidence rather than impression.
